agent_trace.summary: A chest radiograph (CXR) is generally feasible in patients with most metal implants, since standard X-ray imaging uses ionizing radiation and is not contraindicated by metal. The main issue is that metal can create radiopaque shadows or obscure nearby anatomy, but the study can still usually be performed; this is consistent with the retrieved cases showing the chest study itself is a chest X-ray of the thorax.

key_facts: Most metal implants do not prevent obtaining a CXR.
Metal is radiopaque, so implants may appear very bright on X-ray and can overlap chest structures.
A CXR evaluates the lungs, heart, mediastinum, trachea, ribs, clavicles, diaphragms, and pleura.
Implants such as pacemakers, sternotomy wires, spinal hardware, and orthopedic plates are commonly visible on chest radiographs.
If metal obscures a region of interest, additional views or another imaging modality may be considered.
